tasks.how: Write the scope, deliverable length and content and deadline in one place.
tasks.tools: Client call notes, kick-off agenda doc
tasks.check: Scope, audience, deliverable length and deadline are written in one place.

tasks.how: Read the last deck, the methodology, review ingredient measurement sheet and the earlier framework (lifecycle, volume, average engagement, decision).
tasks.tools: Last wave deck, methodology change document, ingredient measurement sheet, Claude
tasks.check: The analyst can explain every column and threshold of the old tracker in their own words.
tasks.output: Short list of what to keep, change and drop

tasks.how: Agree roles and milestones. Set milestones and timelines
tasks.check: Roles, reviewers and milestones are written down and shared.

tasks.how: Collect what is happening in the world, beyond oral care. Search Google and read relevant articles, then scan TikTok and Reddit for conversations, formats and ingredients. Look for wellness and beauty trends crossing into oral care (skinification, oral-gut link, GLP-1, longevity). Log each signal with its source link.; Check what is moving at global level and in adjacent categories (skincare, supplements, beauty) that could reach toothpaste. Compare with the existing list of about 400 ingredients and note what to add or test.
tasks.tools: Google, press articles, TikTok (manual search), Reddit
tasks.check: Each signal has a source link, and single-market signals are flagged as such.

tasks.how: Facets were already built in the client Radarly workspace (426 ingredients, 7 languages). Check that every ingredient on the list has a query, and add the missing ones (agave, amino acids, cranberry) before exporting.
tasks.check: Every ingredient on the list has a working tagged query.

tasks.how: Export volume and engagement for three periods, with the tags included in the export. Because everything was already tagged, no query-by-query manual measurement is needed. Read the handover document from an analyst and an analyst to check the queries that are not working and the ingredients need manual extraction.
tasks.check: Row counts match between volume and engagement files, and a few totals are spot-checked in Radarly.

tasks.task: Pull the search signal from Trajaan
tasks.how: Export the US keyword table (Location = United States, English and Spanish keywords), month by month. Apply the noise rules: other languages, medical terms and off-topic keywords out, brand-led keywords flagged. Count identical variant series once. Load September when Google releases it.
tasks.check: The location is checked (values match a US pull, not a multi-country one) and read-back shows no mismatched keywords.
tasks.output: Search volume per ingredient and month

tasks.how: Set up the workbook: all tags, a Top ~75 shortlist (breakout, early signs, growing), a top ~20/40 featured ingredients, and an Overview of themes and benefit territories, with formulas for growth and decision.
tasks.check: Totals tie back to the exports, there are no formula errors, and every ingredient has a decision.

tasks.how: Save the URLs of interesting TikTok videos while researching (55 unique videos). Give Claude the list of URLs and the column headers wanted in the measurement file. Claude returns a sheet with URL, creator, followers, views, engagement, transcript, hashtags, brands mentioned and more.
tasks.tools: TikTok, Claude, the client’s sample file
tasks.check: Spot-check against the live video: handle, numbers and transcript wording. Verbatims are checked against the audio.

tasks.how: Export volume and engagement for benefits, entry points, and rogue ingredients. And if needed and required by the specific project, also formats and brands.
tasks.check: Make sure queries are working and include all the languages needed for the analysis.

tasks.how: Share the top ingredients with a recommended deep-dive flag.
tasks.check: The client-facing sheet is clean: 75 ingredients, no internal columns.

tasks.how: Decide what story the data tells: benefits-led vs ingredient-led, what changed since previous wave, which benefits and ingredients to dive into and which to watch, and the emerging themes (GLP-1 and dry mouth, oral-gut link, longevity, microplastics).
tasks.tools: Tracker, call notes, desk research, reference decks + Claude, Word, tracker
tasks.check: Each chosen benefit has ingredients, a number, a video and a reason, and the story answers 'so what for the client'.

tasks.how: Take all 13 benefits through selection. Pick relevant ingredients per benefit with one callout, then add brand and product callouts and formats.
tasks.check: The selection rule is stated and the counts reconcile with the tracker.

tasks.how: Work through the layout with Claude Design (lead analyst and second analyst). Try alternatives quickly and re-craft slides as needed. Use reference slides as a starting point.
tasks.check: Each slide answers one question and the order follows the outline.

tasks.how: Claude Design had all the measurement files, so charts were built directly from them: ranked benefit bars, ingredient tables and the Top 10 refresh. A bubble chart judged misleading was replaced.
tasks.check: Every chart number is checked against the tracker, with a footnote where benefits overlap.

tasks.how: Pull videos and stills from the sample for each benefit slide. Claude audits the deck for empty visual slots and builds a gaps list and a shot list.
tasks.tools: Sample sheet, TikTok, video shot list
tasks.check: Each still or GIF links to its TikTok, usage rights are checked, US creators are preferred, and UK or #ad items are labelled.

tasks.how: Claude drafts titles, captions and callouts from the tracker and the outline, in house style.
tasks.check: Numbers match the tracker. No em or en dashes in client copy.

tasks.how: Take the deck from Claude Design into Google Slides, fix layout drift, and do the final visual run-through with the second analyst.
tasks.check: Images, fonts and links are intact on every slide.

tasks.how: Go through every line of copy. Rewrite it in the team's voice: short, direct and quant-forward for a US audience. Remove generic AI phrasing and check that verbatims are exact.
tasks.check: No generic phrasing, no dashes, and every verbatim matches the source.

tasks.how: Check each number against the tracker, replace XX placeholders, verify verbatims against audio, check brand availability (US vs UK), label desk-research items as examples and check house style.
tasks.check: Every number traces to its source and no placeholders remain.

tasks.how: Bring in the senior reviewer once the deck is about 75 to 80% complete (late review avoids rework). Implement feedback. Distinguish AI-generated, AI-assisted and human-authored content where it matters.
tasks.check: Reviewer sign-off.

tasks.task: Share the draft with the client
tasks.how: Send the draft with a short cover note, offer a call, and set a feedback window of about 5 days.
tasks.check: The right link and access are shared, and the feedback date is stated.

tasks.how: Gather comments and group them by slide and type (wording, data, scope). The 5-day window is waiting time, not effort.
tasks.check: Every comment has a status: accept, discuss or decline with reason.

tasks.how: Update slides and, if needed, the tracker. Re-run QC on every number that changed.
tasks.check: Changed numbers re-checked and the feedback list closed.

tasks.how: Deliver the final deck by 30 Oct. Save all files in the shared drive, and update the method decisions log and project notes.
tasks.check: Final deck delivered, files saved, and the method log up to date.
